text: Writing clean code is a crucial skill for any programmer. The primary goal is to make your code readable and easy for others—and your future self—to understand. First, use clear and consistent naming conventions; a variable like `userEmail` is far more descriptive than `x`. Second, break your program into small, focused functions, each with a single responsibility. This not only makes testing simpler but also avoids long and confusing blocks of logic. Ultimately, clean code prioritizes maintainability over cleverness. When you write simple, well-structured code, you save time and effort in the long run because it becomes much easier to fix bugs and add new features.
